text:
R437 — External CPU expert-pool optimization opportunities
Accessed: 2026-10-14
Target: Strata native CPU expert pool, Ryzen 5 5600X / AVX2; active10, NT1, five workers, tasks18.
Scope: read-only audit. This is a candidate list, not evidence of a speedup. No benchmark run or source change was made.

Question and source boundary
The inspected Strata implementation is the source tree at
/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-layer-major-bulk-upload-20261013
(commit 85cb6b1968bd5c2156eed3b10dbb332f92ee95ac).
In ExpertPool::run_split_multi_native, workers and (when configured) issuer drain row ranges for GU, then the caller/issuer iterates the jobs and quantizes each hidden FF vector (native_quant_h / act_quant_any), then workers and issuer drain Down row ranges. The Q step is serial on the caller while workers are parked. Existing phase wall spans include dispatch/wait/drain, so they are not a measurement of worker CPU service. The workload of this audit is five worker threads plus issuer, tasks18, one token and ten active expert jobs. No results below imply that a particular stage dominates this Strata run.

External evidence and fit
1. KTransformers CPU-GPU task scheduling (project source and paper)
   Source: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/blob/main/kt-kernel/python/experts_base.py
   Paper: https://madsys.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/publication/ktransformers-unleashing-the-full-potential-of-cpu/gpu-hybrid-inference-for-moe-models/SOSP25-chen.pdf
   The project submits CPU expert forward work to a WorkerPool and synchronizes at an explicit later point; its source also documents a race if an asynchronous callback's enqueue is not host-observable. The SOSP paper describes decode as a small-token-count regime where CPU/GPU synchronization and overlap overhead become material. This establishes a design precedent, not a result transferable to Strata: KTransformers overlaps CPU work with GPU expert computation and uses a different runtime / CPU. Strata's entire GU→Q→Down path here is CPU-native.
   Candidate A — parallelize the Q stage only if its measured caller CPU service is material: expose jobs/tokens as independent quant tasks to the existing pool, then retain a clear completion barrier before Down consumes each hq vector. For NT1, at most ten jobs are available, so this uses idle worker capacity but may cost a wake/barrier and atomics. Do not infer that overlap from KTransformers proves a win. Keep each hq destination single-writer and preserve exact quantizer, scale/rounding, and job ordering semantics; compare outputs exactly or under the project's existing numerical contract. If the measured Q stage is tiny relative to total layer latency, reject this path.

2. ik_llama CPU and MoE kernel work
   Source: https://github.com/ikawrakow/ik_llama.cpp
   The project documents CPU prompt-processing optimizations for MoE and many quant formats, plus separate AVX/VNNI and decode-related work. Its published changelog does not provide a directly comparable Ryzen 5600X / Strata GU-Q-Down measurement. Much of the cited work is kernel/quant-format specific; it does not justify changing Strata's native quantized weight kernel or quantization format from this evidence.
   Candidate B — treat kernel changes as a measured, format-matched follow-up only if per-thread accounting shows GU or Down compute dominates and a code-level comparison identifies the same weight encoding and AVX2 operations. For the current first pass, retain the existing direct quantized-weight multiply and do not port unrelated formats or AVX-512/VNNI techniques. The reported CPU prompt and CUDA results are not decode results for this workload.

3. llama.cpp CPU scheduling / task grain and SGLang CPU roadmap
   Sources: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c
   https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8281
   ggml's CPU implementation has explicit threadpool barriers, chunk dispatch, and NUMA-affinity handling. SGLang's CPU roadmap calls out split-K for small-output-channel gate projection and separately lists hybrid CPU/GPU MoE offload/pipelining. These sources show that grain, synchronization and CPU topology are workload-dependent concerns. SGLang's roadmap is not a measured result; its AMX/Xeon-oriented tasks are not directly applicable to a single-socket 5600X.
   Candidate C — validate task grain / active worker count against actual service-time data, instead of assuming tasks18 is optimal. A paired tasks 6/18/24 test is already recorded as a prior candidate in R314; do not duplicate it if Main has already queued that comparison. On a 5600X, generic NUMA placement is a poor first bet (single-socket/single-CCD consumer setup); only test pinning or issuer placement if observed migrations or CPU clocks suggest scheduling is the limiting factor.

Not proposed
- Paired GU is excluded: R436 found its benefit is limited to reusing activation loads, with synthetic NT1 slower and NT8 faster; neither result establishes a model-level win here.
- Gather optimization is excluded: prior Zen3 evidence is negative.
- Speculative pipelining of partial GU rows into quantization is excluded because it adds synchronization/data-lifetime complexity without evidence that Q is a critical path.
- Do not change weights, formats, task architecture, or the official measurement path based on these external sources alone.

Minimal Main validation before implementation
1. Use the already planned same official non-bulk stock repeat and existing CPU phase ledger; do not launch another concurrent run. Record GU/Q/Down wall spans plus per-thread CPU service/clock attribution, task counts, worker participation, and issuer idle/service time for the exact active10/NT1/task18 case.
2. If Q is material, prototype Candidate A behind a private experiment, then compare repeat-level decode latency/throughput and correctness against stock. Include the additional barrier/dispatch cost; use same affinity, thermal/power state, and model/prompt.
3. If GU or Down dominates, first identify the precise weight format and hotspot before any kernel port. For task grain, use the already planned R314 A/B if it is not already in the current queue. Report individual samples and correctness/fault results; do not use phase wall spans as CPU-service time.
4. Retain only a candidate that improves repeated official stock measurements without correctness or fault regressions. This report itself contains no measured performance claim.
scope: Source-only; runtime remains unqualified unless a separate Main receipt says otherwise
